descriptionChirho: A poetic compound noun (tsalmaveth) denoting the deepest, most impenetrable darkness, traditionally rendered 'shadow of death.' Used of the valley of deep shadow (Ps 23:4), of darkness in Job's laments (Job 3:5, 10:21-22, 12:22, 16:16, 24:17, 28:3, 34:22, 38:17), of spiritual darkness (Ps 44:20, 107:10,14), and prophetically of those dwelling in darkness (Isa 9:1). Multilingual evidence is uniform: eng 'deep-shadow/shadow-of-death', spa 'sombra de muerte', hin मृत्यु-छाया, arb ظِلِّ الْمَوْتِ, kor 사망의 그늘, swa 'kivuli cha mauti'. The prepositional form (S130140, with lamed 'to/towards shadow of death') is a syntactic variant, not a distinct sense.
